chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, that he was asked: “Are the rites performed without wudu (ablution)?” So he said:
Yes, except for tawaf, for in it there is salat (prayer).

key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكُ: the ritual acts of hajj or pilgrimage rites
key_terms.صَلَاةً: prayer; here indicating that tawaf shares its ruling regarding purity
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can the rites of hajj be performed without wudu (ablution), and is tawaf an exception?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the rites of pilgrimage may be performed without wudu (ablution), except for tawaf. Tawaf is treated distinctly because it carries the ruling of salat (prayer) in this regard, indicating the requirement of ritual purity for it.
